PullRequest.Title: agentHost: add setting to turn off Copilot's Co-authored-by trailer
PullRequest.Body:

Copilot sessions that run in the agent host, like the ones in the Agents window, tell the agent to add this trailer to the commits it makes:

```
Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>
```

It comes from a `<git_commit_trailer>` block that the Copilot runtime puts in the system prompt. The SDK has a session option for it, `coauthorEnabled`, which defaults to on. The agent host never sets it, so the only way to avoid the trailer today is to tell the agent not to add it in every session.

The settings people reach for don't help here. `git.addAICoAuthor` only affects commits made through VS Code's Git UI. The CLI's `includeCoAuthoredBy` is applied by the CLI app rather than the runtime, so SDK-hosted sessions like ours never see it.

This adds `chat.agentHost.copilot.includeCoAuthoredBy` and passes it to the SDK as `coauthorEnabled` when a session is created or resumed.

Some notes:

- The default is `true`, so attribution works the same as today unless you opt out. That matches the CLI and the SDK. Whether it should default to off, or follow the consent flow planned for `git.addAICoAuthor` in #314311, is a product call I've left out of this PR; it only adds the opt-out. The one difference is that the host now always sends the value, so the SDK makes an extra `session.options.update` call after each create and resume. `coauthorEnabled` showed up in the runtime in the same version as `enableScriptSafety`, which we already require at launch, so I don't expect that call to fail anywhere that works today.
- The setting reaches the host through the declarative `agentHost` mirroring, using the default all-hosts scope. `Local` isn't enough. On my machine the Agents window talks to a CLI-launched agent host over a websocket, which counts as a remote target, and `Local` settings never reach it.
- It's application-scoped because a host's config is shared by every window and profile connected to it. As with the other mirrored settings, the last client to write it wins.
- It's applied when a session starts or resumes, so an open chat keeps its current behavior. The host also needs this change. An older one stores the value and ignores it.
- It only covers the agent host's Copilot sessions. The extension-host "Copilot CLI" sessions and the Claude and Codex sessions aren't affected.
- The setting should cover sub-agents too, but the runtime doesn't pass it on yet. I checked the bundled runtime (1.0.92-0) using signed-out BYOK sessions against a local mock model. With `coauthorEnabled: false` the main prompt drops the `<git_commit_trailer>` block, but a `general-purpose` sub-agent's prompt still has it. The SDK doesn't give the host a way to set it per sub-agent (there's no sub-agent hook, and `updateSubagentSettings` only covers things like model and effort), so the fix belongs in the runtime: github/copilot-cli#4576. Once that lands, sub-agents should follow this setting without another VS Code change.

Related: #314311 (see [this comment](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/314311#issuecomment-4468267379)), github/copilot-sdk#1172 (the request for the option, which shipped in github/copilot-sdk#1428), and github/copilot-cli#4576.

## How to test

1. Set `"chat.agentHost.copilot.includeCoAuthoredBy": false`.
2. Start a new Copilot session in the Agents window and ask it to commit something itself, not through a sub-agent.
3. The commit shouldn't have the `Co-authored-by: Copilot` trailer. You can also open `~/.copilot/session-state/<session-id>/events.jsonl` and check that the `system.message` event has no `<git_commit_trailer>` block.
4. Set it back to `true` (or remove it) and start another session. The trailer comes back.

What I ran locally:

- `node test/unit/node/index.js --run src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/copilotSessionLauncher.test.ts`: 95 passing, including the new test, which fails with the launcher change reverted.
- The same runner with `copilotCliConfig.test.ts`, `agentHostConfigurationSync.test.ts` and `agentConfigurationService.test.ts` added: 138 passing.
- `npx eslint` and `build/hygiene.ts` on the changed files: clean.
- `npm run typecheck-client`: no new errors. My checkout doesn't have Electron's typings installed, so there are 370 unrelated `electron` errors, but the list is the same with and without this change.

I haven't done the manual Agents window run above against a dev build.

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The changed config field is on the awaited `createSession` launch path, the mirrored registered default is concretely `true`, and the SDK behavior for this session option is explicitly identified as an extra `session.options.update`. The exact milliseconds vary by host load and transport, but the additional critical-path RPC and its one-per-create cardinality are established.
Findings.PerformanceResource: one serialized JSON-RPC `session.options.update` call to the Copilot runtime subprocess per newly created session
Findings.PerformanceScaling: The cost grows linearly with new session creation count (one additional awaited IPC per create); distinct sessions may initialize concurrently, increasing aggregate runtime RPC load.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: increased latency on the session-launch critical path
Findings.PreviousBehavior: Before this diff, new sessions omitted `coauthorEnabled`, used the SDK's enabled-by-default behavior, and did not issue this option-specific update.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: Every new Copilot session now explicitly sends the SDK-default `coauthorEnabled: true`; the SDK applies this option with an additional `session.options.update` JSON-RPC after session creation, adding an awaited subprocess round trip even when the user did not opt out.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: The added RIGHT line 1146 unconditionally includes `coauthorEnabled` in every built session config. The same diff registers and mirrors the setting with default `true` (`chat.shared.contribution.ts` lines 1742-1747), and configuration sync resolves registered defaults, so ordinary sessions send `true` rather than leaving the field absent.
Findings.Title: Omit the default coauthor option on new sessions
Findings.Impact: Starting a new Copilot Agent Host chat pays an unnecessary subprocess IPC round trip before the session can finish initialization, increasing first-use latency for every default-configured session.
Findings.Evidence: `CopilotAgentSession.initializeSession` awaits `CopilotSessionLauncher.launch` before the session is registered; `_createSession` awaits `plan.client.createSession({...config})`. The added field is therefore on the user-visible session startup critical path. Agent-host configuration sync falls back to registered defaults, so default installations pass `true`. For this SDK option, explicit presence causes a separate `session.options.update` RPC to the Copilot runtime. A newly created session already has the SDK default of enabled, so that RPC performs no state change.
Findings.Recommendation: For `plan.kind === 'create'`, omit `coauthorEnabled` when the effective value is `true` and send it only for the opt-out (`false`). Continue sending an explicit value on resume when needed to override a value persisted by an earlier launch.

Scenarios.Scenario: Create a Copilot Agent Host session with the default attribution setting
Scenarios.CriticalPath: `CopilotAgentSession.initializeSession` awaits launcher creation, which awaits the SDK create path and its option application before the session is registered and usable.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Create a Copilot runtime session through the SDK.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One existing SDK create request plus one newly triggered option-update RPC for each new default-configured session.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The create request already occurred, but its config omitted `coauthorEnabled`.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Both are awaited before launcher completion and session registration.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One per new session when the mirrored value is the default `true`.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No option-specific update occurred; the SDK's enabled default applied.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Adds one awaited runtime round trip before the SDK create operation settles.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of newly created Copilot Agent Host sessions; effective cardinality is one added IPC per create.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: A session lifetime serializes materialization for the same session; different new sessions can initialize concurrently, so each contributes its own runtime RPC.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The effective default `true` is mirrored into host root configuration and read from in-memory state for each launch; no cache or coalescing suppresses the option-specific SDK update across newly created sessions.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the diff always includes the mirrored default, the create path is awaited, and explicit presence causes the SDK option update.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The per-RPC duration depends on subprocess load and transport, and launch already performs other updates; this limits severity but not the existence of the added critical-path round trip.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reportable low-severity regression: an explicit default causes avoidable repeated IPC on every new-session launch.

Scenarios.Scenario: Resume an existing Copilot Agent Host session
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Cold resume is awaited before the chat session can initialize and accept work.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Resume the persisted Copilot runtime session.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One existing resume request per effective cold resume, plus one SDK option-update RPC when `coauthorEnabled` is supplied.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Resume occurred without the host supplying this coauthor option.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The SDK resume and option application complete before launcher finalization.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Apply the current coauthor setting to the resumed session.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one per effective cold resume after same-session coalescing.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Adds a runtime round trip during resume.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of distinct cold session resumes, after per-session coalescing.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Concurrent requests for one session share `resumeDefault`; resumes for distinct sessions may proceed concurrently.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Root configuration is read in memory. Same-session concurrent resumes are coalesced by the session lifetime, but a later cold resume performs the option application again.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for the extra RPC; whether any individual resume could omit it without inspecting persisted state is uncertain.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Most resumed sessions likely retain the enabled default, but the host cannot safely omit `true` when a persisted session may previously have been launched with `false`.
Scenarios.Verdict: No separate finding: the update is needed to make a changed setting override persisted session state, and the actionable avoidable subset is the new-session default path already reported.

Scenarios.Scenario: Connect or reconnect a local or remote Agent Host and mirror configuration
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Host configuration synchronization occurs on connection/reconnection, but the new boolean is carried in an existing patch rather than requiring a new request.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Mirror global VS Code settings to the agent host root configuration.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One existing root-config protocol dispatch per connection/reconnection, with one additional boolean property.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same aggregate patch was sent without this one setting value.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: No additional boundary call; only a negligible payload increase.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of host connections/reconnections, not number of sessions or settings.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: One aggregate dispatch per connection/reconnection; no per-session fan-out is introduced by the setting declaration.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The configuration registry and sync entry list are reused; connect/reconnect builds one aggregate root-config patch containing all applicable settings.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: sync code batches every setting into one patch.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: None material; the added payload is a single boolean and key.
Scenarios.Verdict: No performance regression: the diff adds data to an existing batched IPC rather than adding calls or unbounded work.

Scenarios.Scenario: Toggle attribution while sessions are open, then commit from a session
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Changing the setting does not restart or update active sessions, so no runtime boundary is placed on an active turn or commit path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Send the changed root configuration value to the host.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One existing configuration synchronization action per setting change.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Other mirrored setting changes used the same protocol path; this setting did not exist.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Off the active session/turn critical path.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of user setting changes, realistically rare.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: A configuration change is one root-config update; later session launches follow their existing lifecycle controls.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Open sessions keep their launch-time value; configuration changes update host root state and are consumed only by a later create/resume.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the setting description and launcher-only read establish launch-time application.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: None material for performance; commit generation behavior is prompt/runtime functionality rather than additional host-side work.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable performance issue: active sessions are not eagerly restarted or updated, and no new per-commit host boundary is introduced.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all four changed files and all diff hunks. Traced configuration mirroring, new-session creation, cold resume, active-session setting changes, SDK subprocess RPCs, coalescing, and cache behavior. Submitted one low-severity repeated-work finding for the avoidable default option update on newly created sessions; no regression fix was present to record.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
